title: Next.js: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in Image Optimization API when SVG files are used
description: A memory-related vulnerability in an upstream library used by Next.js for Image Optimization can lead to unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) when processing SVG files on glibc-based Linux systems. This affects Next.js versions from 10.0.0 up to but excluding 15.5.28, and from 16.0.0 up to but excluding 16.4.1. The vulnerability is critical and can be mitigated by upgrading the 'sharp' library to version 0.35.5 or later, which is included in patched Next.js releases.
aiSummary: Next.js uses an upstream library called 'sharp' for image optimization. A memory-related vulnerability in this library can be exploited to achieve remote code execution without authentication when SVG files are processed on glibc-based Linux environments. The issue affects Next.js versions >=10.0.0 <15.5.28 and >=16.0.0 <16.4.1. Upgrading 'sharp' to version 0.35.5 or higher mitigates the vulnerability. Fresh installs of Next.js automatically include the fixed 'sharp' version. The vulnerability has a CVSS 4.0 vector indicating critical severity with network attack vector, low attack complexity, no privileges required, and no user interaction needed.
aiImpact: Successful exploitation allows unauthenticated remote code execution on servers running vulnerable Next.js versions on glibc-based Linux. This can lead to full system compromise. There are no known exploits in the wild at this time.
